chapter: Childhood, family and the sounds of New Orleans
title: Louis Armstrong remembers only the good of New Orleans
summary: Danny says Louis spoke only of the pleasures of New Orleans, not the waif's home.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: That's why when you see Louis Armstrong... Louis Armstrong, when he spoke of New Orleans, he forgot the bad things he suffered as a youngster. Everything to him of New Orleans was the good things. He was fortunate(?) that he could differentiate it, to match(?) my home town. He always spoke of the pleasure out of it, not the time when they locked him up and put him in this waif's home, because they shouldn't have -- or maybe they should have, because he had a weapon. But he was not there shootin' nobody; he was (?) a shooting gun. But he always speaks of the town as the pleasurable thing, and hearing the music all the time.
